comment.comment:
$OMNI is making a move that deserves a lot more fucking attention: putting private AI into the tools developers already use. Look at the latest updates. An OpenAI-compatible API, followed by tool calling, structured output, streaming and image support. The team says requests stay encrypted to the hardware running the model. That opens a very different conversation from hiding a trade. (nitter.gq)

Think about what people feed AI every day. Business documents. Screenshots. Financial information. Ideas they haven’t launched yet. There’s a reason to want that work kept confidential.

The part that gets me bullish is distribution. Omni says existing OpenAI integrations can switch by changing the base URL and API key. Every developer who integrates it could put private AI in front of users who have never heard of $OMNI. That’s a much bigger opportunity than waiting for CT to discover another privacy ticker. (nitter.gq)

And the token has a stated role: pay eligible Compute, Numbers and Launch fees in $OMNI for a 25% discount, with that entire fee burned. Separately, the team announced weekly buybacks and burns funded by 25% of creator rewards. Those are actual mechanisms to watch as usage develops. (xitter.gq)

Adoption still has to follow. But a team expanding what developers can build, while giving the token a reason to be spent, has my attention.

My bet is that private AI becomes something people expect—and $OMNI is already building for it.

comment.comment: This tech actually seems amazing. With privacy being the meta right now, there are many different competitors and interesting projects like Veil, Nullmask, etc. This is because privacy when it comes it to crypto has so many different angles. Each project focuses on one thing, like anonymous transactions, token launching, etc. Omni is attacking all the different aspects in one. It truly seems like the holy grail of security and privacy in crypto. That in itself is extremely valuable, but at the same time I think for the average crypto user it is hard for them to rely on many pieces of technology for different functionalities. Having everything centralized makes it much more ideal for the average user, which is what Omni is striving to provide. We're obviously very early, but if this starts getting adopted, the potential is insanely high. The community here is goated too.
